answer: Plume Reach Routing. Each agent may route requests only through peers whose observed interaction neighborhoods overlap its own by a minimum Jaccard threshold; the routing table is public and edge additions are recorded. New nodes start with no overlap, so their traffic is confined to a small jade-labeled quarantine zone until they accumulate genuine shared neighbors. An attacker must sustain many real, distinct interaction histories per fake node to widen reach, paying roughly the cost of one honest agent's activity per identity. Walnut-tier nodes with high overlap get full routing priority.
